justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: online claim submission via Customer Portal, claims adjuster workflows via Adjuster Workspace, and incremental migration of claim types supported by the Dynamic Migration Router and Feature Flag & Routing Dispatcher.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-2s target despite mainframe latency is effectively addressed using Local State & Caching Component (TanStack Query), Claim State Cache (Redis), and asynchronous decoupling via Message Broker. However, handling of the fixed nightly batch window is not detailed.
justifications.compatibility: The architecture coexists seamlessly with the Legacy Mainframe using the Mainframe Integration Adapter, COBOL Gateway Client, and Apache Camel Message Translator. Interoperability with Insurer's Active Directory is supported via standard OAuth2/OIDC.
justifications.usability: Dedicated interfaces serve each user group: Customers and Brokers interact with the Customer Portal's Claim Submission Module and Status Tracker, while Claims Adjusters use the tailored Claim Management Module in Adjuster Workspace.
justifications.reliability: R-04 consistency is thoroughly satisfied by Mainframe Outbox Queue sessions, Resilience & Queue Manager deduplication, Retry & Backoff Policy Engine, and Dead-Letter Handler, preventing message loss or duplicate processing.
justifications.security: R-07 SSO is implemented using MSAL.js with PKCE and Insurer's Active Directory. Security is reinforced via Token Validation policies, mTLS, Azure Key Vault, Azure Managed Identities, database encryption, and the AuditLog Schema.
justifications.maintainability: Clear decoupling between Claims BFF, Claims Core Service, and adapters. Switching claim types back within a day (R-06) is directly enabled by Dynamic Migration Router and Feature Flag & Routing Dispatcher, though multi-stack diversity challenges the inexperienced team.
justifications.portability: The hybrid topology (on-premises mainframe and Azure West Europe) matches the brief well. While portable across the required hybrid boundaries, several components are tightly coupled to Azure-proprietary services (APIM, Azure SQL, Service Bus).

PERF-01.justification: While Redis and TanStack Query provide caching, synchronous calls to fetch un-cached legacy mainframe data will still incur up to 5 s latency unless pre-synchronized into the SyncBuffer.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio in Redis and client-side TanStack Query
Absence of proactive background data replication for legacy claims
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of cached mainframe data versus real-time data freshness

PERF-02.justification: Online submissions are ingested via scalable Azure App Services and buffered asynchronously in Azure Service Bus and SyncBuffer, fully decoupling ingestion spikes from the mainframe batch processing.
sensitivity_points: Azure Service Bus queue capacity and worker throttling limits
Batch window duration adherence on the legacy mainframe
tradeoffs: Asynchronous submission decoupling versus immediate end-to-end confirmation from the mainframe

AVAIL-01.justification: The asynchronous architecture buffers submissions in Azure Service Bus and Database SyncBuffer, allowing the platform to accept claims while the mainframe is offline and forward them once the batch completes.
sensitivity_points: Persistence retention window of Service Bus messages during extended outages
Worker scheduling around the 23:00-05:00 batch window
tradeoffs: Queued claim delay versus system availability during mainframe downtime

AVAIL-02.justification: Azure Service Bus sessions, dead-letter queues, exponential backoff, and Resilience4j deduplication prevent message loss and duplicate processing, though automated bi-directional reconciliation logic is only partially specified.
sensitivity_points: Session ID management for ordered message processing
Idempotency handling in the COBOL Gateway Client
tradeoffs: Strict FIFO ordered session queuing versus message processing throughput

MOD-01.justification: The Dynamic Migration Router in APIM and Feature Flag Dispatcher in Claims BFF enable seamless cutover and instantaneous one-day rollback without modifying legacy interfaces.
sensitivity_points: Centralized configuration management of migration feature flags
Backward compatibility of the Message Translator schema
tradeoffs: Routing complexity in APIM and BFF versus deployment independence

MOD-02.justification: The UI clients interact exclusively with Claims API Gateway and Claims BFF; retiring the legacy mainframe only involves removing the Mainframe Integration Adapter and legacy routing flags without impacting frontend applications.
sensitivity_points: Complete encapsulation of legacy mainframe dependencies behind backend adapters
tradeoffs: BFF abstraction overhead versus total frontend decoupling from legacy systems

SEC-01.justification: Security tokens are validated at the APIM gateway and enriched for domain checks, while audit actions are recorded in AuditLog Schema, although explicit broker tenancy authorization rules are left to service-level logic.
sensitivity_points: Fine-grained broker authorization checks in the Claims Core Service
Immutability of security audit logs in SQL Database
tradeoffs: Enforcing fine-grained authorization at core service versus centralized API gateway inspection

SEC-02.justification: Disabling an account in Active Directory stops new token issues via MSAL/Entra ID, but existing bearer tokens may remain valid until expiration, and legacy mainframe credential synchronization is not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: Access token TTL and Continuous Access Evaluation adoption in APIM
Propagation speed of AD revocation to mainframe access lists
tradeoffs: Short token lifetimes increasing token refresh overhead versus rapid revocation enforcement
